texts.preamble: State vs Saurabh Dhingra on 18 July, 2025 In The Court Of Sh. Animesh Kumar, Judicial Magistrate First Class-02, Patiala House Courts Court, New Delhi State Vs. Saurabh Dhingra Fir No: 17/2010 P. S Chanakyapuri U/s 336 Ipc & 27/54/59 Arms Act Crc No./ 44778/16 Judgment
texts.facts: At about 4:10 AM, when the accused was exiting the Hotel in the said car, he had fired in the air from a country made pistol near the out gate of the hotel. One empty cartridge was found near the spot. After firing one round from the pistol, the accused fled away from the spot. As per the prosecution, the accused had fired from an unlicensed pistol and endangered the personal safety of the others. 3.After completing the formalities, the investigation was carried out by PS Chanakyapuri and a charge sheet was filed against the accused Saurabh Dhingra for the offence punishable u/s 336 IPC & 27/54/59 Arms Act. Thereafter, cognisance was taken and charge was framed against the accused vide order dated 21.10.2014 for the offence punishable u/s 336 Digitally signed by ANIMESH ANIMESH KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2025.07.19 16:06:18 +0530 IPC and 27/54/59 Arms Act to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. PROSECUTION EVIDENCE 4.In order to prove the guilt of accused, the prosecution examined the following twelve witnesses: Sh. Suresh Singh, deposed as PW-1; Sh. A.P Singh, deposed as PW-2; Retired SI Narender Singh, deposed as PW-3; ASI Naresh Kumar, the Duty Officer, deposed as PW-4; SI Satish Chand, deposed as PW-5; Sh. S R Vats, deposed as PW-6; HS Daya Singh, deposed as PW_7; ASI Subhash Chand, deposed as PW-8; Sh. Ramesh Chand, deposed as PW-9; ASI Raghuveer, deposed as PW-10; HC Vikash Kumar, deposed as PW-11; and HC Ashutosh, deposed as PW-12. 5.PW-1 Suresh Singh deposed that in the intervening night of 27/28 January, 2010, he was working as Security Supervisor at Ashoka Hotel. On that day, he was performing his duty at control room from 9:30 PM to 7:30 PM. At around 2 AM, he had received telephone call from a guard ANIMESH Date: KUMAR 2025.07.19 16:06:29 +0530 who informed that somebody had fired at the main out gate of the Ashoka Hotel and fled away with the car. Thereafter, he reached at the main out gate of the Ashoka Hotel where the guard handed over one empty cartridge to him. He informed the duty officer, Ashoka Hotel regarding the incident. State vs Saurabh Dhingra on 18 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73250334/ 2 6.PW-1 was cross-examined by the Ld. APP for the State as he resiled from his earlier statement. In the cross-examination, he admitted that the date of the incident was intervening night of 27/28 January, 2010. He did not remember as to whether the name of guard was Ramesh Chand who informed him regarding the incident. He denied the suggestion that the name of guard was Ramesh Chand who informed him that one person had fired at the main out gate from vehicle bearing no. DL 1CL 7142 Swift white colour car, and thereafter, fled away from the spot with the said car. He denied the suggestion that he was intentionally deposing falsely in order to save the accused as he was won over by the accused. 7.PW-1 was duly cross-examined by the Ld. Counsel for the accused. In the cross-examination, he stated that he was never called by any of the police officials at police station to enquire about the present case. He also stated that no police officials ever came to him to enquire or to record his statement at any point of time. He also stated that he did not remember ANIMESH Date: KUMAR 2025.07.19 16:06:36 +0530 the name of the security guard. He also stated that he had informed to the security officer in writing Ex. PW-1/A. He denied the adverse suggestions. 8.PW-2 Sh. A.P Singh deposed that in the intervening night of 27/28 January, 2010, he was posted as Manager, Security at Ashoka Hotel. On that day at about 4 AM, his security supervisor Suresh Singh informed him that one person had fired in air at the main out gate of the Ashoka Hotel from Maruti swift car whose number he did not remember. Thereafter he went there. He asked Suresh Singh to check the CCTV footage in order to ascertain the registration number of Maruti swift car as well as manual register at the main out gate and main in gate. After scrutiny, Suresh Singh confirmed the registration number of the white Maruti swift car. Thereafter, he made a report in this regard to the Chief Security Officer Ex. PW-2/A. He handed over empty cartridge with was handed over to him by Suresh Singh to the police in an envelope. He correctly identified the empty cartridge which was produced in the Court in a white colour pullanda sealed with the seal of "SCT". 9.PW-2 was duly cross-examined by the Ld. Counsel for the accused. In the cross-examination, he interalia stated that he did not remember if he had stated in the incident report Ex. PW-2/A that he handed over empty cartridge to the police in envelope which was handed over to him by Digitally signed by ANIMESH ANIMESH KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2025.07.19 16:06:42 +0530 Suresh Singh. He also stated that he did not have any personal knowledge about the present case and he came to know about the same when it was informed to him by Suresh Singh. He also stated that he himself did not make any call to the police. He also admitted that the reception area was covered under the CCTV camera and it could be ascertained from the recording as to who had visited the hotel. He also admitted that the CCTV camera was also installed in the parking of area of the hotel and it could be ascertained as to who who had parked and sat on the driver seat. He also stated that the police did not give any notice u/ s 91 State vs Saurabh Dhingra on 18 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73250334/ 3 Cr.P.C to him to prove the CCTV footage of the oaring area or other parts of the hotel to ascertain the presence of the accused at the hotel. He denied the suggestion that no bullet was ever handed over to him by Suresh Singh at any point of time. He also denied all the other adverse suggestions given by the Ld. Counsel for the accused. 10.PW-3 SI Narender Singh Tyagi deposed that on 07.02.2010, he was posted at Special Staff PS Parliament Street as ASI. On that day, the investigation of the present case was handed over to him. He got the case file and interrogated the accused. On 08.02.2010, he produced you before the concerned Court and moved an application Ex. PW-3/A for conducting your TIP proceeding. However, the accused refused to undergo TIP Digitally signed 5 by ANIMESH KUMAR ANIMESH Date: KUMAR 2025.07.19 16:06:48 +0530 proceeding. During the PC remand, he made efforts to recover the pistol used by the accused in the incident but could not find the same. He recorded the supplementary disclosure statement of the accused Ex. PW-3/C to Ex. PW-3/E. During the investigation, he also recorded the statement of the witnesses and after the completion of the investigation, he had filed the charge-sheet in the Court. He correctly identified the accused in the Court. 11.PW-3 was duly cross-examined by the Ld. Counsel for the accused. In the cross-examination, he interalia stated that he did not remember if he had taken the CCTV footage of the entrance of Ashoka Hotel. He also did not remember if he had given any notice u/s 91 Cr.PC to Ashoka Hotel to supply the CCTV footage if all cameras. He also stated that he did not send the empty cartridge to the FSL. 12.PW-4 ASI Naresh Kumar had registered the present FIR Ex. PW-4/A on 28.01.2010 on the basis of rukka produced by ASI Satish. He also made endorsement on the said rukka Ex. PW-4/B. He was duly cross-examined by the Ld. Counsel for the accused. 13.PW-5 SI Satish Chand was the investigating officer of the present case. He deposed that on 28.01.2010, the investigation in the present case was ANIMESH Date: KUMAR 2025.07.19 16:06:54 +0530 marked to him. He made endorsement on the complaint Ex. PW-5/A and got the present FIR registered. After the registration of the present FIR, he along with Ct. Daya Singh went to Ashoka Hotel and met with the complainant S.R Vats, Chief Security Officer. He prepared the site plan at the instance of the complainant Ex. PW-5/B and seized the empty cartridge produced by the complainant after sealing the same with SCT vide seizure memo Ex. PW-5/C. He also seized the CD containing CCTV footage of the spot produced by the complainant vide seizure memo Ex. PW-5/D. State vs Saurabh Dhingra on 18 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73250334/ 4 He also recorded the statement of the witnesses present at the spot i.e. complainant and the security guards. During the course of the investigation, he found out that the registered owner of the vehicle in question (bearing registration no. DL 1CL 7142 make maruti swift white colour) was Anju Dhingra. He also went to the house of the registered owner and found that the said vehicle was parked there. He interrogated the owner of the vehicle who informed him that on 27/28.01.2010, the accused had taken the said vehicle. The vehicle was seized vide seizure memo Ex. PW-5/E. 14.PW-5 SI Satish Chand further stated that on 07.02.2010, the accused had come to PS Chanakyapuri where he interrogated the accused and arrested him vide arrest memo Ex. PW-5/F. The personal search of the ANIMESH Date: KUMAR 2025.07.19 16:07:00 +0530 accused was also conducted vide search memo Ex. PW-5/G. The accused disclosed his involvement in the present incident and his disclosure statement is Ex. PW-5/H. The accused was also taken to the spot and pointing out memo Ex. PW-5/I was prepared. He was duly cross- examined by the Ld. Counsel for the accused. 15.PW-6 S R Vats that on 28.01.2010, he was posted as Chief Security Officer, Ashok Hotel, Chanakyapuri. On the same day at around 10 AM when he came to the office, A.P Singh who was posted as Security Officer reported to him that at around 4:10 AM, one person had fired in the air from his swift car while going out from the main out gate of the Ashoka Hotel. He also handed over one empty cartridge. Thereafter, he watched the CCTV footage installed in the hotel premise from which it was clearly visible that the fire was made by the said car. The entries were made in the Out register. The security guard had written the registration number of the said vehicle as DL 1C 7142 Swift car of white colour. He gave the present complaint Ex. PW-6/A to the police. He also identified the empty cartridge which was produced in the Court in an envelope where the description of the case was mentioned. ANIMESH Date: KUMAR 2025.07.19 16:07:06 +0530 16.PW-7 HC Daya Singh was also involved in the investigation. He deposed that on 28.01.2010 at around 2:40 PM, the duty officer handed him over one tehrir along with copy of FIR to give to the IO. Thereafter, he reached at the spot i.e. out gate, Ashoka Hotel where he met the complainant SR Vats who had produced empty bullet cover to the IO which was seized vide seizure memo Ex. PW-5/C. IO prepared the site plan at the instance of the complainant in his presence. The complainant also handed over the CD containing CCTV footage to the IO. State vs Saurabh Dhingra on 18 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73250334/ 5 17.PW-8 ASI Subhash Chand deposed that on 08.02.2010, he was posted as Head Constable in Special Staff, New Delhi district. On that day, he joined the investigation with ASI Narender when two disclosure statements of the accused were recorded by the IO i.e. Ex. PW-3/C and Ex. PW-3/D. 18.PW-9 Ramesh Chand deposed that on 28.01.2010, he was posted at gate no. 2, Ashoka Hotel, New Delhi as security guard. On that day at about 4:10 AM, one car bearing no. DL 1CL 7142 make Swift car came in the hotel in which one person was sitting. He looked at the accused in the Court and said that "mujhe lag Raha hai yehi hai." He also deposed that Digitally signed by ANIMESH ANIMESH KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2025.07.19 16:07:17 +0530 the accused put out his right hand from the window of the car and fired from the pistol in the air. He also stated that empty shell was also found at the spot and the same was deposited in the Control office. He also correctly identified the empty shell which was produced in the Court in a white pullanda which was sealed with the seal of SCT. 19.PW-10 ASI Raghuveer was only a formal witness as police remand of the accused was taken in his presence and he along with the IO had gone to the house of the accused situated at H. NO. 2655, Hudson lane, Kingsway Camp where the disclosure statement of the accused was recorded. 20.PW-11 HC Vikash Kumar was also a formal police witness who was involved in the investigation of the present case. The accused had surrendered in his presence and he also witnessed the arrest of the accused and his personal search. He also witnessed the preparation of the pointing out memo Ex. PW-5/I. ANIMESH KUMAR KUMAR 2025.07.19 +0530 21.PW-12 HC Ashutosh was also a formal police witness who was involved in the investigation of the present case. He along with the IO went to the house of Anju Kumari, the registered owner of the vehicle. He stated that notice u/s 133 MV Act was served upon her by the IO and she disclosed that her son was driving the said vehicle at the time of the incident. The offending vehicle was seized by the IO in his presence vide seizure memo Ex. PW-5/W. PW-11 DEFENCE OF THE ACCUSED 22.After examination of all prosecution witnesses , at the request of Ld. APP, the prosecution evidence was closed on 28.02.2025. Thereafter, the statement of accused was recorded u/s 313 Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("Cr.P.C") on 22.03.2025 wherein all the incriminating circumstances State vs Saurabh Dhingra on 18 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73250334/ 6 were put to him which he denied and took a defence that he was falsely implicated in the present case. He also stated that he was identified by the complainant at the instance of the prosecution. He also stated that no independent identification was made by the accused. He also stated that his signatures were taken on a blank papers. Thereafter, defence evidence was closed and final arguments were heard. FINAL ARGUMENTS 24.During the final arguments, the Ld. APP submitted that the prosecution has successfully proved the guilt of the accused in the present case beyond reasonable doubts. The eye witness PW-9 Ramesh Chand had correctly identified the accused in the Court. The empty bullet cartridge was also recovered during the course of the investigation. The vehicle used in the commission of the offence could be clearly seen in the CCTV footage. Hence, the accused should be convicted in the present case.
texts.arguments: 25.Per contra, the Ld. Counsel for the accused, on the other hand, argued that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubts in the present case. It was argued that the identity of the accused was doubtful in the present case in as much as the accused could not be identified properly by the eye witness PW-9. No independent investigation was carried out by the investigating agency to establish the identity of the accused in the present case. Also, the country made pistol from which the firing was allegedly done could not be recovered during the ANIMESH Date: KUMAR 2025.07.19 12 16:07:38 +0530 course of the investigation. Thus, benefit of doubt needs to be extended to the accused. LAW INVOLVED IN THE PRESENT CASE 28.Section 336 of the IPC provides for the offence of doing such acts which endanger human life or safety of others. It reads as under: "Whoever does any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to two hundred and fifty rupees, or with both" 29.Any action that, due to its reckless or negligent nature, has the potential to cause harm or death to another person is an act endangering human life or safety of others. This includes actions that may not necessarily result in injury but have a high risk of doing so. 30.Section 27 of the Arms Act provide punishment for using arms in contravention of provision enshrined u/s 5 & 7 of the Arms Act. Date: 2025.07.19 16:07:45 +0530 regulates the licensing of arms and ammunition, specifically for their manufacture, sale, transfer, and other related activities.
